record.paper_title: Open Questions about Time and Self-reference in Living Systems
record.original_question: What mathematical formalisms and computational tools can model a self-modifying open system that changes its own rules and remains open to its environment, especially when open-endedness requires models and metamodels that can produce level-1 innovations and level-2 transformations rather than only level-0 state variations?

evidence.quote:
Banzhaf et al. [13] consider variation to be a normal property of any dynamical system, and so not the
kind of novelty of interest in open ended systems. So they define an open ended system to be one that
continually produces type-1 and type-2 novelties.

This suggests the route to modelling open ended
self-modifying systems, including living systems, is to use models and languages that themselves have
self-modifying capabilities

What are appropriate mathematical formalisms and computational tools for mod-
elling a self-modifying system that changes its own rules, and is open to its en-
vironment?

artifact.status_search_result: The question is a foundational open research question about modelling open-ended, self-modifying living/open systems. Surveys on open-endedness (Banzhaf et al., Taylor et al.) and works on reflective/rewriting systems address aspects of it, but no broadly accepted mathematical formalism that fully captures level-1 innovations and level-2 model-level transformations is known. Web search did not surface a definitive resolution; the question remains open in the open-ended evolution and artificial life literature.

status_evidence.title: Defining and Simulating Open-Ended Novelty (Banzhaf et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Distinguishes type-0, type-1 and type-2 novelties and argues open-ended systems must continually produce type-1 and type-2 novelties; identifies the modelling challenge as still open.
status_evidence.claim: The challenge of formalising systems producing level-1 and level-2 novelties is treated as an outstanding research problem.

status_evidence.title: Open-Ended Evolution: Perspectives from the OEE Workshop (Taylor et al.)
status_evidence.snippet: Identifies the lack of adequate mathematical and computational frameworks for open-ended, self-modifying systems as a central open problem in artificial life.
status_evidence.claim: No accepted formalism yet exists for self-modifying open-ended systems.
